findings.refactoring: Encapsulate invariant: iterate sorted(source.literals.items()), or state the ascending-offset order on Source.literals in mask_c_like/Source
rationales: normalize_comparison rebuilds a string by slicing source.comparable between literal spans in the order source.literals is iterated. Correct output depends on mask_c_like inserting literal spans in ascending source-offset order, but Source.literals (dict[int, int]) does not promise that order. Sorting the spans makes the helper self-contained and immune to a future refactor of mask_c_like that builds the map out of order.
behaviorRisks: Sorting the keys yields the identical ascending sequence mask_c_like currently produces, so comparable argument strings are unchanged; all V5 self-comparison outcomes stay the same.

rationales: The change adds an ~11-line expect-chain noop scan inline, so scan_typescript now interleaves test discovery, selection scans, and two distinct V5 scans. Extracting the new loop into a helper mirrors java_noops and makes the function a named sequence of steps, each independently testable.
behaviorRisks: Preserve marker ordering (expect markers appended after assertion and selection markers), the exact rule 'V5' and message 'new constant or self-comparing expect assertion', and the violation offsets passed to violation().

findings.refactoring: Remove Dead Code (collapse the redundant two-operand loop to a single pass over left)
rationales: After the guard 'if not left or left != right: return False' both operands are provably identical, so 'for operand in (left, right)' runs the same pure checks twice over the same string. A single pass over left is equivalent and avoids double mask/regex work, making the equality precondition explicit.
behaviorRisks: None; the loop body is pure and left == right after the guard, so checking left once returns the same boolean.

rationales: test_typescript_different_expect_values_pass, test_typescript_different_literal_whitespace_passes, test_typescript_non_pure_equality_calls_pass, and test_typescript_identity_assertions_with_allocated_literals_pass all repeat the same body (base = self.tree("base", {TS_PATH: TS_TEST}); head = self.tree("head", {TS_PATH: TS_TEST.replace("assert.ok(value)", assertion)}); assertEqual(run_check(base, head)[0], 0)). A private helper such as _assert_typescript_replacements_pass(self, assertions) makes each test a one-line call over its assertion tuple, so adding or correcting a pass-case only touches one place.
behaviorRisks: The helper must preserve each test's exact inputs (the TS_TEST template and per-assertion replacement), the subTest(assertion=...) label, and the single assertEqual(run_check(base, head)[0], 0) assertion; no assertion, input, or timing may change.
